Commentary.Commentary: That is it from this game! All to play for in the next. Do join us for the game on the 7th of June at 1020 local (0820 GMT). Till then goodbye.

Andy Balbirnie says he is happy with the way the team played, they bowled well and the chase was a lot more composed. Adds he wanted to stay there till the end and it was satisfying. Adds Stirling is very imprtant to them and he is a big player. Ends by saying he feels they bowled bettre with the new ball, there was oisutre and they did really well.

Pieter Seelaar says it was a good toss to lose, it got better in the second half and 160 was not enough. States he feels Josh bowled really well and kept bowling in the good areas but all the Irish bowlers bowled well. Adds they will look to come back strong in the next game. Ends by saying he knew it was going to be a similar game like the first one but they did not apply themselves well and they did not play that well.

Man of the Match, Josh Little, says he had to turn things around quickly after his injury and the last few months he has worked hard and it has helped him. Mentions he has lost weight and gotten stronger due to which the ball is coming out nicely. States they were gutted after the first game but are pleased with this performance.

Earlier in the day, after electing to bat, the Dutch got off to a good start but once the first wicket fell, the procession began. Young and Little were the pick for Ireland and they kept the hosts down to a total which was easily chased in the end.
The pacers weren’t as threatening as they were in the first game. Seelaar did cause problems after bowling in the middle overs but it was too little too late.
Netherlands needed a few quick wickets but they only got one. Stirling and Balbirnie really eased the pressure with their partnership.
A good win for Ireland and they have levelled the series. To be honest, it was their bowlers who set it up for them. Yes, the wicket is tough but just below 160 was never going to be enough.

OUT! CAUGHT! Stirling has departed and this has come out of nowhere. Against the run of play for sure. Can Netherlands still make a comeback or is it too late?  Floated on off, Stirling comes down the track and looks to hit it over mid on. He has to stretch out for it. He does not get the elevation and hits it straight to Stephan Myburgh at mid on. He makes no mistake. 67 needed in 161.
Commentary.Howout: c Stephan Myburgh b Pieter Seelaar

OUT! BOWLED! Porterfield departs without troubling the scorers and his poor run of form with the willow continues. Terrific bowling from Logan van Beek! He goes full on middle and off, and makes the ball swing back in to Porterfield. The former Ireland skipper looks to defend but tries to get his pad away. The ball goes right between the bat and pad to hit the stumps.

Huge shout for LBW but the umpire says nothing doing. Seems to be going down leg. Full toss on the pads. It comes back in to the southpaw. Porterfield looks to flick but misses and gets hit on the pad. There is a huge shout but the umpire is unmoved.
Much better from Logan van Beek. Good length ball on off and nipping it back in. Stirling defends it to the on side off the inner half of his bat. The batter takes a run.
FOUR! Another loosener and Stirling punishes it yet again! Full outside off, Stirling says thank you very much and creams it through covers again for a boundary,

FOUR! Stirling starts off with a beautiful drive and gets off the mark with a boundary. Overpitched ball around off, Stirling leans forward and creams his drive through covers for a boundary. Ireland are finally up and running.
Logan van Beek to bowl from the other end!
Full toss but Klaassen gets away with it. It is on off and middle, Porterfield pushes it to mid on. Maiden from Klaassen to begin the innings.
Very full around off, Porterfield drives it to the left of short cover. The fielder there dives and saves runs for his side.
Good length ball around off, Porterfield walks down the track and blocks it.
Fuller on off, Porterfield keeps it out.

IN THE AIR AND SAFE! Full ball on middle and leg, Porterfield looks to flick hut turns his bat a little too early. It takes the leading edge and lobs. Luckily for Porterfield it lands away from the bowler and in front of mid on. Is this the luck Porterfield needed?
Klaassen starts with a good length ball that comes in to the southpaw. Porterfield defends it to cover to start off the innings.
